entries.rationale: Record deterministic path-package resolution for additive product-owned workspace crates.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Regenerate Cargo.lock with the pinned toolchain after adding or removing product workspace crates; never hand-merge generated package entries.
semantic_invariants: The lockfile is generated by the pinned Cargo toolchain rather than hand-edited.
Existing external dependency versions and checksums are unchanged by provider crate registration.
Removing product-owned crates removes only their path-package lock entries.

entries.rationale: Register additive product-owned memory-provider crates without changing upstream feature defaults or package behavior.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove only the additive product workspace member lines when the provider layer is removed; preserve all upstream workspace members and settings.
semantic_invariants: The repository remains one virtual Rust workspace with resolver 3 and edition inherited from workspace.package.
Provider crates are additive workspace members and do not replace or reconfigure any upstream crate.
Default TraceDecay features and production behavior remain unchanged until the explicit default-off composition mount.

rules: An active entry must correspond to an actual diff against the immutable upstream floor.
Every actual upstream-owned existing-file diff must have exactly one active entry.
A retired entry remains historical evidence but cannot authorize a current diff.
An exception entry must name one exception zone, one versioned ADR, rejected alternatives, policy revision, and rollback plan.
The entry line budget may be lower than the global per-file cap but never higher without a policy revision.

purpose: One reviewed record for every intentional edit to an upstream-owned existing file, preserving rationale, semantic invariants, verification, and the path back to upstream convergence.

snapshot.observed_state: The product branch changes only additive workspace membership and generated path-package lock entries; provider API, fabric, Native adapter, topology-neutral NCM boundary, and provider-neutral conformance harness remain product-owned.
